record.one_liner: AI-powered meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes voice conversations.
record.auth_notes: The Public REST API, available to Enterprise customers, uses static personal bearer tokens. The official remote MCP server, available on all plans, uses OAuth2.
record.access_notes: While the full REST API and webhooks are restricted to the Enterprise plan, Otter provides an official, self-serve MCP server that is available on all plans, including the free 'Basic' tier. This allows developers to build integrations without needing to contact sales.
record.api_notes: The REST API allows programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details. The separate, self-serve MCP server provides tools for user info, search, and fetching meeting data.
record.mcp_notes: Otter hosts an official remote MCP server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp. It is available on all plans, including the free tier, and uses OAuth for authentication.

evidence.quote: Otter.ai is a meeting assistant platform that provides real-time transcription, recording, summaries, and searchable notes for voice conversations, allowing teams and developers to capture meeting content, automate follow-up workflows, and integrate conversation data into collaboration and productivity tools.
All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication... include your api key in the authorization header for every request: authorization: bearer your_api_key
The server supports OAuth Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), so the client registers itself automatically — no developer-portal app, client_id , or client_secret to create.
getting started: otter's public api is available for all enterprise workspaces. if you do not see this feature for your workspace, contact your otter account manager.
otter api & webhooks

otter.ai’s public api provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your otter account.
OpenAPI/Swagger specs. -

backed by its official remote MCP server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp (launched March 13, 2026).

notes:
### **Verification Notes**

**subcategory**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: "AI Meeting Assistant"
*   **Reasoning**: Multiple sources describe Otter.ai as a meeting assistant. Capterra's profile calls it a "cloud-based meeting assistant". A review from July 2026 also refers to it as an "AI Meeting Assistant".
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://www.capterra.com/p/173153/Otter-ai/](https://www.capterra.com/p/173153/Otter-ai/): "Otter.ai is a cloud-based meeting assistant that automatically records, transcribes, and summarizes voice conversations in real time."

**one_liner**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: "AI-powered meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes voice conversations."
*   **Reasoning**: This is a consistent description across multiple sources. Capterra states it "automatically records, transcribes, and summarizes voice conversations in real time." TechRadar says it is an "AI-powered transcription tool designed to convert speech into text in real time, useful for meetings, interviews, and lectures."
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://www.capterra.com/p/173153/Otter-ai/](https://www.capterra.com/p/173153/Otter-ai/): "Otter.ai is a cloud-based meeting assistant that automatically records, transcribes, and summarizes voice conversations in real time."

**auth_methods**: WRONG
*   **Value**: `["bearer_token", "oauth2"]`
*   **Reasoning**: The first-pass record is correct that these two methods exist, but they apply to different services. The REST API uses bearer tokens, while the MCP server and some integrations use OAuth2. The documentation for the REST API explicitly states it uses bearer tokens. The documentation for the MCP server states it uses OAuth. A separate set of API docs for a different Otter product (for restaurants) also mentions OAuth 2.0 with client credentials. Since both are official, both should be listed.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API): "All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication."
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server): "Security: All access is OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions."

**primary_auth**: WRONG
*   **Value**: `oauth2`
*   **Reasoning**: The definition of `primary_auth` prefers OAuth2 if the vendor offers public OAuth apps for multi-tenant integrations. The official MCP server is available on all plans (including free) and uses OAuth. This makes it the most accessible and modern authentication method for building a multi-tenant integration. The REST API's bearer token is restricted to Enterprise plans.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server): "Security: All access is OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions. Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize."
    *   [https://merge.dev/mcp/otter-ai](https://merge.dev/mcp/otter-ai): "Authentication, OAuth. Tool surface, Defined by Otter.ai. Vendor docs, help.otter.ai. Authentication. Otter.ai authenticates over OAuth."

**auth_notes**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: "The Public REST API, available to Enterprise customers, uses static personal bearer tokens. The official remote MCP server, available on all plans, uses OAuth2."
*   **Reasoning**: This is an accurate summary. The official API documentation confirms the REST API uses bearer tokens and is for Enterprise workspaces. The official MCP server documentation confirms it uses OAuth and is available on all plans, as shown on the pricing page.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API): "Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces... All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication."
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server): "Connect AI models to Otter using Model Context Protocol (MCP)... Security: All access is OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions."
    *   [https://otter.ai/pricing](https://otter.ai/pricing): The pricing page lists "new Otter MCP server" under the "Basic" (free) plan.

**access**: WRONG
*   **Value**: `self_serve_free`
*   **Reasoning**: While the first-pass record correctly identifies that the REST API is `partner_or_sales`, it misses that the MCP server is self-serve and available on the free plan. According to the definitions, if *any* developer can get working credentials at no cost, the access is `self_serve_free`. The pricing page from the initial scrape and a third-party analysis confirm the MCP server is on the free "Basic" plan.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://otter.ai/pricing](https://otter.ai/pricing): The pricing page lists "new Otter MCP server" under the "Basic" (free) plan.
    *   [https://www.spokenly.com/blog/otter-ai-pricing/](https://www.spokenly.com/blog/otter-ai-pricing/): "The free tier includes integrations with Zoom, MS Teams, and Google Meet, plus the Otter MCP server."

**access_notes**: WRONG
*   **Value**: "While the full REST API and webhooks are restricted to the Enterprise plan, Otter provides an official, self-serve MCP server that is available on all plans, including the free 'Basic' tier. This allows developers to build integrations without needing to contact sales."
*   **Reasoning**: The original notes were partially correct but incomplete. The REST API and webhooks are indeed gated behind the Enterprise plan. However, the key detail is the existence of the self-serve MCP server on the free plan, which changes the overall access story from `partner_or_sales` to `self_serve_free`.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API): "Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces."
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/16340013323415-Workspace-Webhooks](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/16340013323415-Workspace-Webhooks): "This content is available for the Otter Enterprise plan and may require admin permissions."
    *   [https://otter.ai/pricing](https://otter.ai/pricing): The pricing page lists "new Otter MCP server" under the "Basic" (free) plan.

**api_styles**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: `["rest"]`
*   **Reasoning**: The official API documentation describes a standard REST API with endpoints like `GET /conversations`.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API): "Explore the available API endpoints, grouped by type... GET /conversations Use this endpoint to list conversations for the authenticated user."

*   **Source**:
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/36130822688279-Otter-ai-Public-API): "Otter.ai’s public api provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your otter account."

**api_notes**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: "The REST API allows programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details. The separate, self-serve MCP server provides tools for user info, search, and fetching meeting data."
*   **Reasoning**: The first part of the note is a direct quote from the API documentation. The second part about the MCP server is confirmed by third-party documentation which lists the available tools.

*   **Reasoning**: The initial record was incorrect. While I could not find an OpenAPI spec for the Otter.ai *transcription* API, search results show documentation for a different product, also named Otter (otterab.com), which is for A/B testing and *does* have an OpenAPI spec. It's crucial to distinguish between the two. For the Otter.ai transcription product, no official OpenAPI spec was found.
*   **Source**: No source found for an Otter.ai (transcription) OpenAPI spec.

**webhooks**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: `true`
*   **Reasoning**: The official API documentation confirms the existence of webhooks and recommends them for building integrations. A separate help article specifies that webhooks are an Enterprise plan feature.
*   **Source**:

The API documentation does not mention a sandbox. The unrelated Otter A/B testing product mentions `oab_test_` keys, but clarifies it's an "organizational label, not a behavioral split."
*   **Source**: No source found.

**mcp**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: "official"
*   **Reasoning**: Otter.ai maintains official documentation for its MCP server on its help center. The pricing page lists the "Otter MCP server" as a feature on all plans. Multiple third-party sources also refer to the official, vendor-hosted MCP server.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server): "Connect AI models to Otter using Model Context Protocol (MCP)."

**mcp_notes**: CONFIRMED
*   **Value**: "Otter hosts an official remote MCP server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp. It is available on all plans, including the free tier, and uses OAuth for authentication."
*   **Reasoning**: Multiple sources confirm the official MCP server URL and that it uses OAuth. The pricing page and other sources confirm its availability on the free plan.
*   **Source**:
    *   [https://merge.dev/mcp/otter-ai](https://merge.dev/mcp/otter-ai): "Server URL, https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp. Authentication, OAuth."
    *   [https://www.manufact.com/mcp/otter-ai](https://www.manufact.com/mcp/otter-ai): "The MCP URL is https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect."

**verdict**: WRONG
*   **Value**: `ready_now`
*   **Reasoning**: The definition of `ready_now` is "public docs + self-serve creds; a developer could build it this week." Otter.ai meets this criteria via its official MCP server, which is documented on the help center and available on the free plan, allowing any developer to sign up and get started. The previous verdict of `needs_outreach` was based only on the Enterprise-gated REST API and was incorrect.
*   **Source**:
